newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh probes 1995 arms airdrop in India.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh probes 1995 arms airdrop in India.

text.p: Bangladesh police are investigating suspected local involvement in a mysterious 1995 airdrop of arms in India's West Bengal state, newspapers on Thursday quoted Home (interior) Minister Rafiqul Islam as saying.
"The investigation has been initiated at the request of the (Bangladesh) foreign ministry," Islam told parliament late on Wednesday.
Boxes of weapons dropped by a foreign plane on Purulia in West Bengal state in December 1995 were reported to have labels inscribed with names of senior Bangladeshi defence officials.
Indian newspapers at the time said the consignment might have been destined for Bangladesh but mistakenly dropped in India.
Indian authorities have yet to shed any light on the drop.
Islam said the then Bangladesh government had failed to take up the case, but he did not say why the present administration had taken nearly a year since coming to office to order a probe.
Analysts say allegations by the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) that Indian intelligence agencies had opened an office in Bangladesh to investigate the case had prompted the new probe.
Islam said the allegations were false. "No foreign agency is investigating the isssue here," he said on Wednesday.
